methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Shinkei, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $30M to date, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public peer across the sector. The private peer set spans seed through Series B stages and includes firms such as Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression anchors to the $30M raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $60M. Peer-median triangulation across the five most relevant comps—spanning Seed to Series B—produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The dispersion reflects heterogeneity in stage and maturity within the peer set; notably, Humanoid at Series A stages at $1.4B, while earlier-stage Walden Robotics sits at $1.1B.

The two methods imply a wide triangulated range: $51M (low), $855M (median), and $1.9B (high). The stage-progression method likely underweights Shinkei's relative competitive position within an increasingly capital-intensive sector, while the peer-median approach may overweight later-stage comparables. Key uncertainties include Shinkei's specific unit economics, technology differentiation relative to named peers, and the timing and terms of the next financing event. A defensible range would center in the $200M–$400M band pending granular due diligence on product-market fit and burn rate.
